subtype: Approach: explaining the pivot to the team openly [Action]
passage:
On Monday morning Uday pulled the whole team into the meeting room and put a sheet on the wall screen: monthly users, money in, money out, the line going the wrong way. "This is where we are," Uday said. "And this is what I want to change."
Then came a slide for each role. The mobile work would move to a clinic dashboard. Support and sales would sit together. Parul's testing job would grow to cover the new product, with the same pay and a new review date.
Parul asked three questions about the numbers and then nodded slowly. By Friday two engineers had handed in notice, politely and with thanks. Everyone else stayed and started on Monday's plan.

qa.q: What did Uday put on the wall screen at the start of the meeting?
qa.a: Uday put up a sheet of monthly users, money in and money out.

qa.q: What was Parul feeling during the meeting?
qa.a: Parul was wary at first and then steadier: asking three questions about the numbers and then nodding slowly shows the doubts were being answered.

qa.q: What could Uday do to help the two engineers who left?
qa.a: Uday could offer a fair handover period and a reference, so the departure is respectful and the team's work continues smoothly.

qa.q: How might the two engineers who left have seen the meeting?
qa.a: They probably respected the openness even though the new plan was not for them, since they left politely and with thanks.

grounding: The passage shows a founder sharing the numbers, reasons and each role's future openly, so that most of the team commits despite two departures.

subtype: Approach: explaining the pivot to the team openly [Action]
passage:
"Everyone, I'll show you the numbers first, then the decision." Damini clicked to the chart. "Four hundred schools tried the parent app. Eleven pay. But sixty schools use the fee-reminder feature every week, and forty have asked if they can pay for just that."
"So we're switching to fee reminders?" Rehana asked from the back.
"Yes. Here's what that means for each of you. Rehana, design stays, but you'll simplify, not add. Backend team: most of you move onto reminders. Two of the mobile roles will shrink, because the parent app goes into maintenance. I'll talk to those two of you today, one to one."
"Why not give the parent app another quarter?"
"Because we've given it three. I'd rather tell you the truth now than in six months."
Two weeks later, two mobile engineers had taken jobs elsewhere. Rehana stayed. "At least I knew exactly why," she said.

qa.q: How many schools asked to pay for just the fee-reminder feature?

qa.a: Rehana felt respected and reassured, because she knew exactly why the change was happening.

qa.q: What else could Damini do for the two engineers whose roles shrank?
qa.a: Offer references and help with their job search, and keep them informed so they leave on good terms.

qa.q: How might the two mobile engineers have experienced the meeting?
qa.a: They likely felt disappointed and uncertain, but at least heard the news openly before the one-to-one talks.

grounding: It shows a founder sharing the numbers, the reasons for a pivot and what happens to each role, so two engineers leave but the rest commit because the reasoning was visible.

subtype: Approach: explaining the pivot to the team openly [Action]
passage:
I put off the all-hands for two weeks because I was scared of the faces. When I finally stood in front of our nine people, Urmila, my co-founder, stood next to me with the laptop.
I didn't soften it. I showed them the churn chart for the consumer app, down every month since October, and then the one bright line: small shops using our stock alerts every single day. I said, "We're pivoting to stock alerts for shops. Here's why." Then I went role by role. Support would stay. Two marketing roles would end, with six weeks' notice and help finding new jobs. Engineering would shrink the app to one feature.
Two engineers left within a month; one told me they'd hoped to build consumer products. The other seven stayed. Later Urmila told me what one of them said in the kitchen: "I don't love it, but I can see the reasoning. That's enough."
— Devika

qa.q: What did the one bright line on the chart show?
qa.a: Small shops using the stock alerts every single day.

qa.q: Why did Devika put off the all-hands for two weeks?
qa.a: Devika was scared of seeing the team's faces and dreaded delivering hard news.

qa.q: What made the meeting work despite the bad news?
qa.a: Devika showed the real numbers, explained the reasons and went role by role, so people could see the reasoning.

qa.q: How might the engineer who hoped to build consumer products have felt?
qa.a: That engineer probably felt disappointed that the work they cared about was ending, which is why they left.

grounding: It shows a founder openly sharing the numbers, the reasons for the pivot and each role's future, so two engineers leave but the rest commit.
